title: World General Geography
description: 330 original geography questions covering world rivers, mountains, deserts, oceans, straits, islands, borders, landmarks, and currencies.
author: QuizRooms

questions.prompt: Which river is the longest in Africa and flows northward into the Mediterranean Sea?
questions.explanation: The Nile stretches roughly 6,650 km from East Africa through Sudan and Egypt to the Mediterranean.

questions.prompt: Which river carries the largest volume of water discharge on Earth?
questions.explanation: The Amazon discharges about 209,000 cubic meters of water per second into the Atlantic Ocean.

questions.prompt: Which is the longest river in Asia?
questions.explanation: The Yangtze River in China is approximately 6,300 km long.

questions.prompt: Which river flows through London?
questions.explanation: The River Thames runs for 346 km through southern England and central London.

questions.prompt: Which river runs through Paris?
questions.explanation: The Seine flows 777 km through northern France, including the heart of Paris.

questions.prompt: Which river forms much of the border between the United States and Mexico?
questions.explanation: Known as the Rio Bravo in Mexico, the Rio Grande defines the Texas–Mexico border.

questions.prompt: Which waterfall on the border of Zambia and Zimbabwe is locally known as Mosi-oa-Tunya?
questions.explanation: Mosi-oa-Tunya means 'The Smoke That Thunders' in the Lozi language.

questions.prompt: Which country is home to Angel Falls, the world's highest uninterrupted waterfall?
questions.explanation: Angel Falls plunges 979 meters from Auyán-tepui in Venezuela's Canaima National Park.

questions.prompt: Which man-made waterway connects the Mediterranean Sea directly to the Red Sea?
questions.explanation: Opened in 1869, the Suez Canal in Egypt is one of the world's busiest maritime trade routes.

questions.prompt: Which man-made canal connects the Atlantic Ocean to the Pacific Ocean across Central America?
questions.explanation: Completed in 1914, the Panama Canal uses lock systems to lift ships across the Isthmus of Panama.

questions.prompt: Which is the largest freshwater lake in the world by surface area?
questions.explanation: Lake Superior covers about 82,100 sq km on the Canada–United States border.

questions.prompt: Which is the deepest lake in the world?
questions.explanation: Located in Siberia, Russia, Lake Baikal reaches a maximum depth of 1,642 meters.

questions.prompt: Which saltwater body is the largest enclosed inland body of water on Earth?
questions.explanation: Despite its name, the Caspian Sea is an endorheic basin covering about 371,000 sq km.

questions.prompt: Which hypersaline salt lake in northern Utah is the largest saltwater lake in the Western Hemisphere?
questions.explanation: The Great Salt Lake is a remnant of prehistoric Lake Bonneville and is far saltier than the ocean.

questions.prompt: Which river is the longest in Europe?
questions.explanation: The Volga flows about 3,530 km through western Russia into the Caspian Sea.

questions.prompt: Which European river flows through more countries (ten) than any other river in the world?
questions.explanation: The Danube passes through or borders 10 countries from Germany to the Black Sea.

questions.prompt: Which river flows through the Grand Canyon in Arizona?
questions.explanation: Over millions of years, the Colorado River carved the Grand Canyon.

questions.prompt: Which is the largest lake in Africa by surface area?
questions.explanation: Lake Victoria is shared by Tanzania, Uganda, and Kenya and is a primary source of the White Nile.

questions.prompt: Niagara Falls lies on the border between the United States and which other country?
questions.explanation: Niagara Falls separates Ontario, Canada, from New York State, USA.

questions.prompt: Which river flows through Baghdad, Iraq?
questions.explanation: Together with the Euphrates, the Tigris formed ancient Mesopotamia.

questions.prompt: Which river flows through Cairo, Egypt?
questions.explanation: Cairo sits near the apex of the fertile Nile Delta.

questions.prompt: Which South American waterfall system straddles the border of Argentina and Brazil?
questions.explanation: Iguazu Falls consists of about 275 individual drops along the Iguazu River.

questions.prompt: Which is the highest navigable lake in the world, located in the Andes?
questions.explanation: Lake Titicaca sits at 3,812 meters above sea level on the Peru–Bolivia border.

questions.prompt: Which river is the longest in the United States?
questions.explanation: At about 3,767 km, the Missouri River is slightly longer than the Mississippi River.

questions.prompt: Which river is sacred in Hinduism and flows through northern India and Bangladesh?
questions.explanation: The Ganges rises in the western Himalayas and empties into the Bay of Bengal.

questions.prompt: Which major river flows through Vienna, Budapest, and Belgrade?
questions.explanation: The Danube passes through four national capitals: Vienna, Bratislava, Budapest, and Belgrade.

questions.prompt: Which is the second-deepest lake in the world, located in East Africa's Rift Valley?
questions.explanation: Lake Tanganyika reaches a depth of 1,470 meters and is the world's longest freshwater lake.

questions.prompt: Which river is the only major river in the world to cross the Equator twice?
questions.explanation: The Congo River arches north of the Equator before curving back south to the Atlantic.

questions.prompt: Which river forms the iconic horseshoe-shaped 'Horseshoe Bend' and feeds Lake Mead?
questions.explanation: Hoover Dam impounds the Colorado River to create Lake Mead.

questions.prompt: Which river is the longest in Australia?
questions.explanation: The Murray River runs about 2,508 km from the Australian Alps to the Southern Ocean.

questions.prompt: Which Asian river is nicknamed 'China's Sorrow' due to its historic devastating floods?
questions.explanation: The Yellow River (Huang He) carries massive amounts of yellow loess silt.

questions.prompt: Which river flows through six Southeast Asian countries before emptying into the South China Sea?
questions.explanation: The Mekong runs through China, Myanmar, Laos, Thailand, Cambodia, and Vietnam.

questions.prompt: Which European river flows through Cologne, Basel, and Rotterdam?
questions.explanation: The Rhine is one of Europe's most vital industrial shipping corridors.

questions.prompt: Which is the only Great Lake located entirely within the United States?
questions.explanation: The other four Great Lakes all straddle the US–Canada border.

questions.prompt: Which river flows through Rome?
questions.explanation: Ancient Rome was founded on the banks of the Tiber River.

questions.prompt: Which is the longest river in Italy?
questions.explanation: The Po runs 652 km eastward across northern Italy into the Adriatic Sea.

questions.prompt: Which canal in northern Germany links the North Sea to the Baltic Sea?
questions.explanation: The Kiel Canal saves ships hundreds of nautical miles around the Jutland Peninsula.

questions.prompt: Which Canadian river is the longest in Canada?
questions.explanation: The Mackenzie River flows northward for 1,738 km (4,241 km with tributaries) into the Beaufort Sea.

questions.prompt: Which river flows through Florence, Italy?
questions.explanation: The Ponte Vecchio spans the Arno River in Florence.

questions.prompt: Which river empties into the Persian Gulf after the Tigris and Euphrates join?
questions.explanation: The Shatt al-Arab is formed by the confluence of the Tigris and Euphrates in southern Iraq.

questions.prompt: Which lake in Kazakhstan is split into a freshwater western half and a saltwater eastern half?
questions.explanation: A narrow strait separates Lake Balkhash's fresh western basin from its saline eastern basin.

questions.prompt: Which river forms the border between much of Thailand and Laos?
questions.explanation: The Mekong forms most of the natural boundary between Laos and Thailand.

questions.prompt: Which major river flows through Bangkok?
questions.explanation: The Chao Phraya flows south through central Thailand into the Gulf of Thailand.

questions.prompt: Which river in South Africa forms part of the border with Namibia?
questions.explanation: The Orange River is South Africa's longest river, flowing west to the Atlantic Ocean.

questions.prompt: Which lake in Scotland is the largest by water volume in the British Isles?
questions.explanation: Because of its great depth (230 m), Loch Ness holds more water than all lakes in England and Wales combined.

questions.prompt: Which is the largest lake by surface area in the United Kingdom?
questions.explanation: Lough Neagh in Northern Ireland covers about 392 sq km.

questions.prompt: Which river flows through the city of Prague?
questions.explanation: The famous Charles Bridge crosses the Vltava River in Prague.

questions.prompt: Which river is the longest in the Iberian Peninsula?
questions.explanation: The Tagus runs 1,007 km through Spain and Portugal, reaching the Atlantic at Lisbon.

questions.prompt: Which waterfall in Guyana is one of the world's largest single-drop waterfalls by volume?
questions.explanation: Kaieteur Falls drops 226 meters in a single sheer plunge on the Potaro River.

questions.prompt: Which lake in Central Asia has shrunk by over 80% since the 1960s due to river diversion?
questions.explanation: Diversion of the Amu Darya and Syr Darya for irrigation caused one of the worst environmental disasters.

questions.prompt: Which river flows through Pakistan and gave India its name?
questions.explanation: The Indus flows from Tibet through Jammu & Kashmir and Pakistan into the Arabian Sea.

questions.prompt: Which river forms the dramatic 'Three Gorges' in China?
questions.explanation: The Three Gorges Dam on the Yangtze is the world's largest hydroelectric power station by capacity.

questions.prompt: Which narrow Greek canal cuts through the Isthmus of Corinth?
questions.explanation: Completed in 1893, the Corinth Canal separates the Peloponnese from mainland Greece.

questions.prompt: Which is the largest lake in Central America?
questions.explanation: Lake Nicaragua is famous for containing freshwater bull sharks.

questions.prompt: Which river flows through Warsaw, Poland?
questions.explanation: The Vistula is Poland's longest river at 1,047 km.

questions.prompt: What is the highest mountain on Earth above sea level?
questions.explanation: Mount Everest stands 8,848.86 meters above sea level on the Nepal–Tibet border.

questions.prompt: Which mountain range separates Europe from Asia?
questions.explanation: The Ural Mountains run roughly north–south through western Russia.

questions.prompt: What is the longest continental mountain range in the world?
questions.explanation: The Andes extend about 7,000 km along the western coast of South America.

questions.prompt: What is the highest mountain in Africa?
questions.explanation: Kilimanjaro in Tanzania is a dormant stratovolcano standing 5,895 meters high.

questions.prompt: Which iconic snow-capped stratovolcano is the highest mountain in Japan?
questions.explanation: Mount Fuji rises 3,776 meters on the island of Honshu, southwest of Tokyo.

questions.prompt: Which is the second-highest mountain on Earth above sea level?
questions.explanation: Located in the Karakoram range on the Pakistan–China border, K2 reaches 8,611 meters.

questions.prompt: Which mountain range forms the natural border between France and Spain?
questions.explanation: The Pyrenees stretch from the Bay of Biscay to the Mediterranean Sea, containing Andorra.

questions.prompt: What is the highest mountain in North America?
questions.explanation: Denali in Alaska reaches 6,190 meters above sea level.

questions.prompt: Which famous volcano destroyed Pompeii and Herculaneum in 79 AD?
questions.explanation: Mount Vesuvius overlooks the Bay of Naples in southern Italy.

questions.prompt: Which is Europe's tallest active volcano, located on the island of Sicily?
questions.explanation: Mount Etna stands over 3,350 meters tall and erupts frequently.

questions.prompt: What is the highest mountain in the Alps?
questions.explanation: Mont Blanc rises 4,808 meters on the French–Italian border.

questions.prompt: Which mountain range runs down the spine of Italy?
questions.explanation: The Apennines stretch about 1,200 km from northern to southern Italy.

questions.prompt: What is the highest mountain in South America?
questions.explanation: Located in Argentina, Aconcagua reaches 6,961 meters — the highest peak outside Asia.

questions.prompt: Which mountain in Ecuador has the summit farthest from the center of the Earth?
questions.explanation: Because Earth bulges at the Equator, Chimborazo's peak is farther from Earth's center than Everest.

questions.prompt: Measured from its oceanic base to its summit, which Hawaiian volcano is the tallest mountain on Earth?
questions.explanation: Mauna Kea rises over 10,200 meters from the Pacific Ocean floor.

questions.prompt: What is the highest mountain in Europe (when including the Caucasus)?
questions.explanation: Mount Elbrus in southern Russia stands 5,642 meters above sea level.

questions.prompt: What is the highest mountain on mainland Australia?
questions.explanation: Mount Kosciuszko in the Snowy Mountains of New South Wales reaches 2,228 meters.

questions.prompt: Which mountain range stretches across Morocco, Algeria, and Tunisia?
questions.explanation: Mount Toubkal (4,167 m) in Morocco is the highest peak of the Atlas Mountains.

questions.prompt: What is the highest mountain in Antarctica?
questions.explanation: Vinson Massif in the Sentinel Range stands 4,892 meters high.

questions.prompt: Which famous pyramid-shaped Alpine peak sits on the border between Switzerland and Italy?
questions.explanation: The Matterhorn rises 4,478 meters above Zermatt and Breuil-Cervinia.

questions.prompt: Which plateau in Central Asia is known as the 'Roof of the World'?
questions.explanation: Averaging over 4,500 meters in elevation, the Tibetan Plateau is the world's highest and largest plateau.

questions.prompt: What is the highest mountain in Canada?
questions.explanation: Located in Yukon's Kluane National Park, Mount Logan reaches 5,959 meters.

questions.prompt: Which Indonesian volcano erupted catastrophically in 1883, creating one of the loudest sounds in recorded history?
questions.explanation: The 1883 Krakatoa eruption triggered massive tsunamis in the Sunda Strait.

questions.prompt: Which Indonesian volcano's 1815 eruption caused the 'Year Without a Summer' in 1816?
questions.explanation: Tambora's VEI-7 eruption on Sumbawa is the largest volcanic eruption in recorded history.

questions.prompt: What is the third-highest mountain in the world?
questions.explanation: Kangchenjunga rises 8,586 meters on the border of Nepal and Sikkim, India.

questions.prompt: Which mountain range forms the main highland spine of Iran?
questions.explanation: The Zagros Mountains stretch about 1,600 km across western Iran into Iraq and Turkey.

questions.prompt: What is the highest mountain in the United Kingdom?
questions.explanation: Ben Nevis in the Scottish Highlands stands 1,345 meters above sea level.

questions.prompt: What is the highest peak in Spain, located on the Canary island of Tenerife?
questions.explanation: Mount Teide is a volcano rising 3,715 meters above sea level.

questions.prompt: Which active volcano is the southernmost active volcano on Earth, located in Antarctica?
questions.explanation: Mount Erebus on Ross Island features a persistent convecting lava lake.

questions.prompt: Which mountain range runs across Central and Eastern Europe through Romania, Slovakia, Poland, and Ukraine?
questions.explanation: The Carpathians form a 1,500 km arc across Central and Eastern Europe.

questions.prompt: Which mountain in Turkey is traditionally associated with Noah's Ark?
questions.explanation: Mount Ararat is Turkey's highest peak at 5,137 meters.

questions.prompt: What is the highest peak in Greece, famous in ancient mythology as the home of the gods?
questions.explanation: Mount Olympus rises 2,917 meters near the Aegean coast.

questions.prompt: Which mountain range runs along eastern North America from Alabama to Newfoundland?
questions.explanation: The Appalachians are among the oldest mountain ranges on Earth.

questions.prompt: Which is the highest active volcano in the world, located on the Argentina–Chile border?
questions.explanation: Ojos del Salado reaches 6,893 meters in the Andes.

questions.prompt: What is the highest mountain in Mexico?
questions.explanation: Pico de Orizaba (Citlaltépetl) is a 5,636-meter stratovolcano.

questions.prompt: Which mountain range in South Africa is known as 'uKhahlamba' in Zulu?
questions.explanation: The Drakensberg forms the eastern escarpment of southern Africa.

questions.prompt: Which large volcanic plateau covers much of central and southern India?
questions.explanation: The Deccan Traps were formed by colossal volcanic eruptions about 66 million years ago.

questions.prompt: What is the highest mountain in New Zealand?
questions.explanation: Aoraki / Mount Cook stands 3,724 meters in the Southern Alps of South Island.

questions.prompt: Which US volcano in Washington State erupted explosively on May 18, 1980?
questions.explanation: The 1980 eruption blew off the top 400 meters of Mount St. Helens.

questions.prompt: Which mountain range separates the Indian subcontinent from the Tibetan Plateau?
questions.explanation: The Himalayas contain most of Earth's peaks exceeding 8,000 meters.

questions.prompt: Which peak in the Karakoram is nicknamed 'Killer Mountain' for its historically high fatality rate?
questions.explanation: Nanga Parbat (8,126 m) in Pakistan is the ninth-highest mountain in the world.

questions.prompt: Which mountain range forms the spine of Scandinavia between Norway and Sweden?
questions.explanation: Also called the Scandes, they run 1,700 km along the Scandinavian Peninsula.

questions.prompt: What is the highest peak in the Rocky Mountains?
questions.explanation: Mount Elbert in Colorado stands 4,401 meters above sea level.

questions.prompt: What is the highest mountain in the contiguous United States?
questions.explanation: Mount Whitney in California's Sierra Nevada reaches 4,421 meters.

questions.prompt: Which mountain range in Central Asia stretches across Afghanistan and northern Pakistan?
questions.explanation: The Hindu Kush forms a western extension of the Himalayan mountain system.

questions.prompt: What is the largest hot desert in the world?
questions.explanation: The Sahara covers roughly 9.2 million sq km across North Africa.

questions.prompt: What is the largest desert overall on Earth when including polar deserts?
questions.explanation: Antarctica receives very little precipitation and spans about 14.2 million sq km.

questions.prompt: Which desert in northern Chile is the driest non-polar desert on Earth?
questions.explanation: Parts of the Atacama sit in a double rain shadow between the Andes and Chilean Coast Range.

questions.prompt: Which vast cold desert spans southern Mongolia and northern China?
questions.explanation: The Gobi is a rain-shadow desert created by the Tibetan Plateau blocking Indian Ocean moisture.

questions.prompt: Which desert covers much of southern Africa, including most of Botswana?
questions.explanation: The Kalahari is a semi-arid sandy savanna spanning about 900,000 sq km.

questions.prompt: Which ancient coastal desert along the Atlantic is located primarily in Namibia?
questions.explanation: The Namib is considered the world's oldest desert and is famous for towering red sand dunes at Sossusvlei.

questions.prompt: What is the largest tropical rainforest on Earth?
questions.explanation: The Amazon spans nine South American nations, with about 60% inside Brazil.

questions.prompt: Which biome, also known as the boreal forest, is the world's largest terrestrial biome?
questions.explanation: The taiga forms a circumpolar belt of coniferous forest across Canada, Alaska, Scandinavia, and Russia.

questions.prompt: What is the imaginary line of latitude at 0 degrees that divides Earth into Northern and Southern Hemispheres?
questions.explanation: The Equator passes through 13 countries across South America, Africa, and Asia-Oceania.

questions.prompt: Through which London district does the Prime Meridian (0° longitude) pass?
questions.explanation: The Royal Observatory in Greenwich established the international Prime Meridian in 1884.

questions.prompt: At roughly what latitude is the Tropic of Cancer located?
questions.explanation: The Tropic of Cancer marks the northernmost latitude where the sun can appear directly overhead.

questions.prompt: What is the world's largest sand desert (erg), located in the southern Arabian Peninsula?
questions.explanation: The Empty Quarter spans parts of Saudi Arabia, Oman, the UAE, and Yemen.

questions.prompt: Which desert straddles the border between northwestern India and eastern Pakistan?
questions.explanation: The Thar Desert is the world's most densely populated desert.

questions.prompt: Which US desert is home to Death Valley, the lowest point in North America?
questions.explanation: Badwater Basin in Death Valley sits 86 meters below sea level.

questions.prompt: Which desert in northwestern China sits inside the Tarim Basin?
questions.explanation: The Silk Road skirted the northern and southern edges of the shifting dunes of the Taklamakan.

questions.prompt: What is the world's second-largest tropical rainforest after the Amazon?
questions.explanation: The Congo Basin rainforest spans six Central African nations.

questions.prompt: What is the name of the horseshoe-shaped zone around the Pacific Ocean known for frequent earthquakes and volcanoes?
questions.explanation: Roughly 75% of the world's active volcanoes and 90% of earthquakes occur along the Ring of Fire.

questions.prompt: What geological phenomenon causes the eastern side of a mountain range to be much drier than the windward side?
questions.explanation: Moist air cools and precipitates as it rises over mountains, leaving dry descending air on the leeward side.

questions.prompt: Which warm Atlantic ocean current keeps Western Europe significantly milder than similar latitudes in Canada?
questions.explanation: The Gulf Stream transports warm tropical water northeastward across the Atlantic.

questions.prompt: Which cold ocean current flows northward along the western coast of South America?
questions.explanation: The Humboldt Current creates rich marine fisheries and contributes to the dryness of the Atacama.

questions.prompt: Which Australian desert is the largest desert on the Australian continent?
questions.explanation: The Great Victoria Desert covers about 348,750 sq km across Western and South Australia.

questions.prompt: What is the name of the permanently frozen subsoil found across Arctic tundra regions?
questions.explanation: Permafrost remains at or below 0°C for at least two consecutive years.

questions.prompt: Which huge salt flat in southwestern Bolivia is the world's largest salt flat?
questions.explanation: Salar de Uyuni spans over 10,000 sq km and turns into a giant mirror after rain.

questions.prompt: Which desert in southwestern United States and northwestern Mexico is the only natural habitat of the saguaro cactus?
questions.explanation: The Sonoran Desert covers parts of Arizona, California, and Sonora, Mexico.

questions.prompt: What is the name of the seasonal wind shift that brings heavy summer rains to South and Southeast Asia?
questions.explanation: The summer monsoon is driven by differential heating between the Asian landmass and the Indian Ocean.

questions.prompt: Which massive coral reef system off the northeast coast of Australia is the largest on Earth?
questions.explanation: The Great Barrier Reef stretches over 2,300 km in the Coral Sea.

questions.prompt: Which rainforest in Queensland, Australia, is one of the oldest surviving tropical rainforests on Earth?
questions.explanation: The Daintree is estimated to be over 135 million years old.

questions.prompt: What is the name of the treeless, vast flat plains region of Argentina and Uruguay?
questions.explanation: The fertile Pampas are a major center for agriculture and cattle ranching.

questions.prompt: Which famous African savanna ecosystem in northern Tanzania hosts the annual Great Migration of wildebeest?
questions.explanation: Over a million wildebeest migrate cyclically between Tanzania's Serengeti and Kenya's Maasai Mara.

questions.prompt: What is the name of the semi-arid transition belt stretching across Africa just south of the Sahara?
questions.explanation: The Sahel runs from Senegal on the Atlantic to Eritrea on the Red Sea.

questions.prompt: Which tectonic boundary runs down the center of the Atlantic Ocean and surfaces on land in Iceland?
questions.explanation: Iceland straddles the divergent boundary between the North American and Eurasian plates.

questions.prompt: What is the name of the periodic warming of eastern Pacific equatorial waters that alters global weather patterns?
questions.explanation: El Niño weakens Pacific trade winds, causing droughts in some regions and heavy rainfall in others.

questions.prompt: Which vast inland delta in Botswana empties into the Kalahari Desert instead of the sea?
questions.explanation: The Okavango River fans out into a seasonal wetland oasis in northern Botswana.

questions.prompt: Which huge desert in Turkmenistan covers about 70% of the country?
questions.explanation: The Karakum contains the burning Darvaza gas crater, nicknamed the 'Door to Hell'.

questions.prompt: Which desert in eastern Iran has recorded some of the highest land surface temperatures on Earth?
questions.explanation: Satellite measurements in the Dasht-e Lut have exceeded 70°C on bare dark rock surfaces.

questions.prompt: Which famous geological valley stretches over 6,000 km from Lebanon through East Africa to Mozambique?
questions.explanation: Tectonic plates pulling apart created the Great Rift Valley's chain of lakes and volcanoes.

questions.prompt: What term describes a funnel-shaped coastal estuary drowned by rising sea levels, as seen at the mouth of the Amazon?
questions.explanation: An estuary is a partially enclosed coastal body where freshwater rivers meet ocean tides.

questions.prompt: What term describes a long, narrow, deep sea inlet carved by ancient glaciers, common in Norway?
questions.explanation: Norway's Sognefjord is over 200 km long and more than 1,300 meters deep.

questions.prompt: What is the name of the dry, warm downslope wind that descends the eastern side of the Rocky Mountains?
questions.explanation: Chinook winds can raise winter temperatures by 20°C or more in a single day.

questions.prompt: Which line of longitude at roughly 180° marks where the calendar date changes by one day?
questions.explanation: The International Date Line zigzags through the Pacific Ocean to keep island nations on the same day.

questions.prompt: Which is the largest and deepest ocean on Earth?
questions.explanation: The Pacific covers about one-third of Earth's total surface area.

questions.prompt: Which is the smallest and shallowest of the world's five major oceans?
questions.explanation: The Arctic Ocean surrounds the North Pole and is partly covered by sea ice year-round.

questions.prompt: What is the deepest known point in Earth's oceans?
questions.explanation: Challenger Deep in the Mariana Trench plunges nearly 10,935 meters below sea level.

questions.prompt: Which narrow strait separates Spain from Morocco and connects the Atlantic Ocean to the Mediterranean Sea?
questions.explanation: At its narrowest point, the Strait of Gibraltar is only about 14 km wide.

questions.prompt: Which Turkish strait divides Istanbul between Europe and Asia and links the Black Sea to the Sea of Marmara?
questions.explanation: The Bosphorus is one of the world's narrowest strategic waterways for international shipping.

questions.prompt: Which strategic strait connects the Persian Gulf to the Gulf of Oman?
questions.explanation: A major share of the world's seaborne petroleum passes through the Strait of Hormuz.

questions.prompt: Which waterway separates England from France at its narrowest point?
questions.explanation: The Strait of Dover within the English Channel is roughly 34 km wide.

questions.prompt: Which strait separates Russia from Alaska?
questions.explanation: At its narrowest, the Bering Strait is about 85 km wide between Siberia and Alaska.

questions.prompt: Which sea lies between the Arabian Peninsula and northeastern Africa?
questions.explanation: The Red Sea is linked to the Mediterranean by the Suez Canal and to the Indian Ocean by Bab-el-Mandeb.

questions.prompt: Which sea has no land boundaries and is defined entirely by four Atlantic ocean currents?
questions.explanation: The Sargasso Sea is named for the free-floating Sargassum seaweed that gathers in its gyre.

questions.prompt: Which strait between the Malay Peninsula and Sumatra is one of the busiest shipping lanes in the world?
questions.explanation: The Strait of Malacca connects the Indian Ocean to the South China Sea.

questions.prompt: Which sea lies between Italy and the Balkan Peninsula?
questions.explanation: Venice, Dubrovnik, and Split all sit along the Adriatic coast.

questions.prompt: Which sea lies between Greece and Turkey and contains thousands of islands?
questions.explanation: The Aegean Sea is an arm of the Mediterranean dotted with the Cyclades and Dodecanese.

questions.prompt: Which is the largest bay in the world by surface area?
questions.explanation: The Bay of Bengal covers about 2.17 million sq km in the northeastern Indian Ocean.

questions.prompt: Which bay in eastern Canada is famous for having the highest tidal range in the world?
questions.explanation: Tides in the Bay of Fundy can rise and fall by up to 16 meters.

questions.prompt: Which strait at the southern tip of South America was first navigated by Ferdinand Magellan in 1520?
questions.explanation: The Strait of Magellan separates mainland South America from Tierra del Fuego.

questions.prompt: Which stormy body of water lies between South America's Cape Horn and Antarctica?
questions.explanation: The Drake Passage is notorious for fierce winds and massive waves in the Southern Ocean.

questions.prompt: Which strait separates Yemen on the Arabian Peninsula from Djibouti and Eritrea in Africa?
questions.explanation: Bab-el-Mandeb translates roughly to 'Gate of Grief' and links the Red Sea to the Gulf of Aden.

questions.prompt: Which sea separates Australia from New Zealand?
questions.explanation: Named after Dutch explorer Abel Tasman, the Tasman Sea is about 2,000 km wide.

questions.prompt: Which strait separates the North Island and South Island of New Zealand?
questions.explanation: Cook Strait is about 22 km wide at its narrowest point.

questions.prompt: Which strait separates mainland Australia from Tasmania?
questions.explanation: Bass Strait connects the Indian Ocean's Great Australian Bight to the Tasman Sea.

questions.prompt: Which sea lies between the Korean Peninsula and mainland China?
questions.explanation: Silt from the Yellow River gives the shallow Yellow Sea its golden hue.

questions.prompt: Which sea borders Ukraine, Romania, Bulgaria, Turkey, Georgia, and Russia?
questions.explanation: The Black Sea connects to the Mediterranean via the Bosphorus and Dardanelles.

questions.prompt: Which sea in northern Europe is bordered by Sweden, Finland, Estonia, Latvia, Lithuania, Poland, Germany, and Denmark?
questions.explanation: The Baltic Sea is one of the world's largest brackish inland seas.

questions.prompt: What is the deepest trench in the Atlantic Ocean?
questions.explanation: The Milwaukee Deep in the Puerto Rico Trench reaches about 8,376 meters.

questions.prompt: What is the deepest trench in the Indian Ocean?
questions.explanation: Also known as the Sunda Trench, it plunges over 7,290 meters south of Indonesia.

questions.prompt: Which strait connects the Sea of Marmara to the Aegean Sea?
questions.explanation: Known in antiquity as the Hellespont, the Dardanelles lies along the Gallipoli Peninsula.

questions.prompt: Which narrow strait separates Sicily from mainland Italy?
questions.explanation: The Strait of Messina is just 3.1 km wide at its narrowest point.

questions.prompt: Which strait separates Papua New Guinea from northern Australia?
questions.explanation: Torres Strait is about 150 km wide and dotted with coral reefs and islands.

questions.prompt: Which body of water separates Iran from the Arabian Peninsula?
questions.explanation: The Persian Gulf is a shallow extension of the Indian Ocean.

questions.prompt: Which gulf lies between Sweden and Finland?
questions.explanation: The Gulf of Bothnia is the northernmost arm of the Baltic Sea.

questions.prompt: Which huge inland sea in northeastern Canada is frozen for much of the year?
questions.explanation: Hudson Bay is the second-largest bay in the world after the Bay of Bengal.

questions.prompt: Which sea lies between the United Kingdom, Norway, Denmark, Germany, and the Netherlands?
questions.explanation: The North Sea is rich in offshore wind farms and oil/gas fields.

questions.prompt: Which sea surrounds the Caribbean islands between North and South America?
questions.explanation: The Caribbean Sea covers roughly 2.75 million sq km.

questions.prompt: Which strait separates Greenland from Iceland?
questions.explanation: The Denmark Strait contains the world's largest underwater waterfall of cold dense water.
